Command: Priests shall eat the flesh of the guilt offering
Summary: The command: Priests shall eat the flesh of the guilt offering (Leviticus 7:6). The trespass offering was most holy; every male among the priests ate it in the holy place.
Commandment: Priests shall eat the flesh of the guilt offering, as prescribed in Leviticus 7:6.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: The trespass offering was most holy; every male among the priests ate it in the holy place — a ceremonial law of priestly eating. Its goal was to keep the guilt offering's flesh within the sanctuary, eaten by the priests who bore the people's guilt in the rite. It did not address a particular evil; its work was order and provision, not restraint. The most holy food stayed in the most holy place, and the priests who ate it shared in the atonement's work.
